evidence.quote: We expect to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes—as well as our maximum-employment mandate—are achieved.

We indicated that we will continue to increase our holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and our holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $40 billion per month
for those sectors that have been most adversely affected by the pandemic, price increases remain subdued.
the economy has turned out to be more resilient in adapting to the virus, and more responsive to monetary and fiscal policy support, than many predicted.
the prospects for the economy in 2021 and beyond have brightened and the downside risk to the outlook has diminished.
We are committed to using our full range of tools to support the economy and to help ensure that the recovery from this difficult period will be as robust as possible.

parsed.rationale: The speech reiterates strongly accommodative, outcome-based guidance for zero rates and continued asset purchases under the new average-inflation-targeting framework, with subdued inflation. An upgraded outlook and diminished downside risks temper the dovishness somewhat.
